newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn seeks to exonerate Germans who fought Nazis.
newsitem.headline: Bonn seeks to exonerate Germans who fought Nazis.

text.p: The German government said on Wednesday it planned new legal measures to speed up the rehabilitation of anti-Nazi resistance fighters who were convicted by Nazi courts.
"More than half a century after the end of World War Two, verdicts are still in force which were clearly based on Nazi injustice," Justice Minister Edzard Schmidt-Jortzig said in a statement.
"We cannot expect the relatives of former resistance fighters, among others, to have to restore the honour of those affected themselves."

Germany's 16 federal states are currently responsible for overturning the verdicts of Nazi courts where these were clearly unjust. But the procedure is a legal minefield which has left many of the most glaring cases still unsettled.
The need for action was highlighted most recently by the case of Dietrich Bonhoeffer, a Protestant clergyman executed at a concentration camp in 1945 for opposing Hitler.
Prosecutors applied in March last year for his high treason conviction to be quashed.
After months of investigation, a Berlin court ruled it could not pardon Bonhoeffer as a Bavarian law had already exonerated him and his co-conspirators in 1946.
But adding to the confusion, a Munich court ruled in 1951 that the sentences were in accord with laws which had been in force at the time.

Last year the state prosecutor responsible for dealing with Nazi justice in Berlin ordered his staff to check all such cases to see which convictions may already have been lifted in the immediate postwar period, when allied powers and fledgling regional states were passing laws on the issue.

Bonhoeffer, a leading member of the dissident "Confessing Church" banned during the Third Reich, worked with anti-Hitler army officers and travelled to neutral Sweden in 1942 to discuss secret coup plans with a British bishop.
He was arrested in 1943 after urging clergymen actively to oppose Hitler, whom he branded the anti-Christ.

After a coup against Hitler failed on July 20, 1944, the Nazis discovered Bonhoeffer's links to the conspirators and sent him to Buchenwald concentration camp. He was later sent to Flossenbuerg camp in Bavaria, where he was hanged on April 9, 1945.
